subject: Hearthwell launch: throttle forecast & product action items
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-06-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Hearthwell launch: incoming traffic forecast + temporary throttle ask

Team — forwarding Hearthwell's launch details and the attached forecast. They are targeting a phased rollout starting 2026-07-01 with a public beta ramp over two weeks. Key asks from their side: a temporary ingress quota increase to handle peak demo traffic and a short warmup window for KV caching.

Quick summary of their forecast (attachment):
- Day 1 public beta: 7k requests across the day; 95th percentile burst windows ~120 req/min for 10–15m
- Peak weekend load expected on Day 6: sustained 180 req/min for ~1h, with 400 req/min microbursts for ~2m
- Expected median prompt length ~350 tokens; some multi-call chat flows hit 1.2k tokens total

Specific asks for Redwood: temporary quota bump for 72 hours around launch, a recommended routing profile for low-latency chat, and any guidance on model variant fallbacks if we throttle. They also attached a CSV with minute-level projection.

What I need from you: 
- Marcus: product-level blockers or configuration changes we should propose (model variants, fallback policy).
- Stephanie: ops feasibility for a 3-day quota uplift and any warmup suggestions (KV cache, prefill recommendations).
- Laura: CS/solutions notes and whether we should join their runbook call.

I'd like a short sync (20m) later today to align. Karthik will own comms with Hearthwell.

Thanks,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: hearthwell_traffic_sheet.csv (csv)]
[Attachment: product-ask-summary.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hearthwell launch: incoming traffic forecast + temporary throttle ask

On 2026-06-22 Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — forwarding Hearthwell's launch details and the attached forecast.

Thanks Naomi — skimmed the CSV, a few product items to flag before we commit to any SLA-level exceptions:

1) Model variant and fallback behavior
- If they need low latency, recommend using rw-lite-004 for chat frontends and rw-large-001 as fallback. We should confirm semantics if we auto-fallback to a quantized variant (quality delta needs acceptance).

2) KV cache warmup
- For chat flows that reuse context, prefix caching will help. Recommend a 30–60 minute prefill with synthetic traffic to prime KV shards. This is standard, but we'll need clearance from ops to generate that traffic.

3) Rate-limiting policy for microbursts
- We can allow short microburst windows (up to 5m at 3x nominal) but require queueing for sustained periods. If Hearthwell expects recurring 400 req/min microbursts, we should bake in a retry/backoff guidance.

4) Telemetry & regressions
- Ask Hearthwell to provide a small eval set (10–20 prompts) so we can detect quality regressions if fallback happens.

I'll prepare a two-page 'product ask' doc with options (fast path vs safe path) and trade-offs by EOD.

- Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Product Manager — Serving

[Link: https://drive.redwood.com/prod-asks/HW-launch]

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hearthwell launch: incoming traffic forecast + temporary throttle ask

On Tue, Jun 22, 2026 at 10:05 Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com> wrote:
> If they need low latency, recommend using rw-lite-004 for chat frontends...

We can support a scoped 72-hour quota uplift with conditions. Summary of constraints and proposed mitigations: 

- Capacity scope
  - Max provisional ingress uplift: +200% of current pilot quota, capped at an absolute ingress of 250 req/min per account over the uplift window. This maps to the conservative side of their Day 6 projection.
  - If actual sustained load exceeds 250 req/min for >15 minutes, automatic soft-throttle will engage and we will fallback to queued requests with 429s + Retry-After.

- Warmup recommendation
  - We will approve a 45-minute synthetic warmup window starting 30 minutes before launch. Ops will run a prefill job that simulates typical session patterns to populate KV shards.

- Routing / fallback policy
  - We'll route to rw-lite-004 as primary; if CPU/GPU contention arises, fallback to rw-quant-002 (quantized) with a quality note to the CS team. Product should prepare the fallback notices and the eval set Marcus mentioned.

- Observability & guardrails
  - Enable 1m granularity tracing for this account and set alerts on 95th latency and error rate increases. If errors spike >3x baseline, ops will auto-revoke uplift and notify sales + product.

Next steps: 
- I can provision the uplift today if product signs off on the fallback variant and if Sales gets written acceptance from Hearthwell acknowledging possible fallback quality changes.
- Laura: can you confirm CS will have an on-call for the launch window?

Stephanie Nguyen
Infrastructure Ops Lead, Redwood Inference

[Attachment: uplift_provisioning_template.txt (txt)]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Emma Clarke <emma@hearthwell.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hearthwell launch: incoming traffic forecast + temporary throttle ask

Emma — thanks for the quick turnaround on the forecast. Per internal alignment: 

- Redwood can provision a scoped 72-hour ingress uplift starting 2026-07-01 09:00 PT with the constraints Stephanie outlined (max 250 req/min ceiling, automated soft-throttle beyond sustained thresholds).
- Product (Marcus) will provide the fallback variant documentation and a short eval set by 2026-06-25 so Hearthwell can sign-off.
- Ops (Stephanie) will run a 45-minute warmup 30 minutes before launch; we will coordinate exact timing next week.

Action items for Hearthwell:
1) Please confirm acceptance of the fallback plan (expect minor quality delta if quantized fallback runs).
2) Share 10–20 representative prompts for the eval set by EOD 2026-06-25.
3) Confirm a point of contact for runbook execution during the 72-hour window.

I'll schedule a 20m alignment call tomorrow to finalize timing. Thanks team — will loop in the runbook once Hearthwell confirms.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

On a separate note for internal ops: Naomi, please share the CSV link in the HubSpot deal so we have an auditable record.
